answers.question: At the final card, "you" appears for the only time in the game (Welcome, you. / You are not on file. / Please wait, you.). What should the player feel at that word?
answers.answer: It should feel degrading, like how they call him a number instead of his name. That “you” is holding a lot of weight and malice. It’s literally belittling his identity by referring to him in the only way which gives him not characteristics. You doesn’t have gender, it’s doesn’t have a name, it’s universal used to give a command to someone beneath you. Example: Hey you, get me something. See how you makes them sound like an object

answers.question: Doc 1 says there is no correct answer and no escape: three ways to stop being a person (§0, §9.1), and on replay the spine shows agency was cosmetic (§1.3, reading 2). Do you still stand by both?
Who is Ninety-Nine for first?
What should this teardown help you decide next?
answers.answer: How to merge, and work back in the old blender and Higgsfield sets. My understanding of game design as increased since I’ve worked with “Who did it” so I’m confident those old pieces can be re used

answers.question: Doc 4 §14 bans non-diegetic UI: the only things left over the room are the EXIT sign (styled as a fire exit, it files you as PENDING REVIEW) and the sound toggle. Is even EXIT one too many?
The choice labels (TAKE A SEAT / STAY STANDING, PART THE CURTAIN / TRY THE DOOR) stand in the room over the place to walk to, in the company's typeface. Should they ever lie?
Phone or desktop first: which do you play Ninety-Nine on yourself?

The sets are built: build_rooms.py writes rooms.json (367 KB, 31 rooms and connectors). The choices are hand-edited: scenes.json names each scene's rooms, thresholds and beats. Is that split the right one?
Who should be able to author a new scene later?
answers.answer: Someone working from the data alone

answers.question: The beat vocabulary has grown to 34 keys the director reads (caption, swing, display, breath, footfall, ride, sit, actor…). Where would you stop it?
answers.answer: Let it grow, but document each

answers.question: Should duplicate rooms change a little, like the backrooms' duplication effect? (asked in conversation, after the options for room drift were laid out)
answers.answer: yes, ask chapter 3 questions, i like all four options you mentioned and id also like get rid of the two screenoverlays. a cool random screen effect would be cool but id have to see options.

answers.question: Room drift (the backrooms copy effect): which should Ninety-Nine use?
answers.answer: i dont want to get rid of any scenes that already exists only change the duplicate rooms for option 4.,1. Aliases drift via `unseen`,2. Alias drift lists,3. Drift tied to fracture,4. H as a corrupted copy of C

answers.question: With the two fracture overlays gone (the opposite render's colour bleed and the fixed '99' slip), which random screen effect should replace them? Each fires rarely, more often as fracture rises, and never on a threshold.
Retiring the mini-games (2026-10-03) for walked thresholds was the largest change. What made you decide it?
answers.answer: the designs sucked and felt more like chores. Worst design ideas I've had to date. none of it felt themed either it was like a Band-Aid for the lack of game play

answers.question: Friction now comes from how he moves (hesitating, doubling back between thresholds) and feeds only fracture. Should the player ever be told that it counts?

Ninety-Nine's tests run in a browser page opened by hand (12 case files), with an optional headless runner and an autopilot that plays whole games. For Right Door you chose CI on every push. Same here?
The 48 Hz drone (C7) is one oscillator from the lobby doors to the final card, never restarted, detuning ~4 cents per scene. Is it the game's most important system?
You play on desktop. What is the slowest machine it must run well on?
The building's mood in three words?
Which canon rule (C1 to C8) would you defend if you had to break all the others? (C7, the drone, is already on the table.)
answers.answer: C1, C4. i like the low poly look but its more ps1, I'm looking to up it to a ps2 scale or even a higher quality modern "low to mid poly"

answers.question: Doc 1 §9.3 asks whether Harlowe deserves more: today SAW_HARLOWE adds a desktop, a manifest row and one extra lowercase line on the ending card, "a haunting instead of an easter egg". What is your answer now?
With C1 moving to low-to-mid poly, where should the company's new props come from?
The generated stills and clips of the video era were removed when the game became 3D-only. Is there anything from that era you miss?
answers.answer: the look of the stills, the transitions, the endings as films. id like to take a much more hands on editing approach when adding them back

answers.question: If the drone goes, what should the building sound like when nothing is happening?
answers.answer: music, sfx, and the rooms tone, utilized to create different moments and envelop the player in the environments

answers.question: The game went from generated video (Sept) to a continuous 3D walk (Oct 1–3). Looking back, was the video era a detour, or a necessary sketch?
Which decision would you make differently with what you know now? (options: the mini-games; generating before designing; the parallel pipelines; nothing yet)
answers.answer: all of the above, except the last

answers.question: The game was built in AI sessions: four specs, then pull requests and review passes with dated amendments. Was that faster, or did the reviews cost more than they saved?
answers.answer: ive got no answer for this one i dont understand the question

answers.question: Simpler version: you built Ninety-Nine by writing four design documents first, then having Claude sessions build it, with you reviewing each change. When the game changed direction (video → 3D walk, mini-games → walking), the documents got 'amendment' notes instead of being rewritten. Do the four documents still help you, or are they in the way now?
answers.answer: i honestly just used them as a reference for growth, i used them to build the game, got claude to amend them, and keep them around bc it shows the growth. failing is a real delight when you can look back and see the strides you took. ive i havent read much of anything but the responses claude gives me, the readme, and actually testing my creation. i played it, my peers played it on my computer, and the designs of both of these games taught me what i know today

about: The owner's answers to the teardown briefs, verbatim, in the order given. Appended by `udgt.py record`; never generated or edited.
